"""Lens B: content-free composition of the clone's index (counts and path labels only; no text)."""
import collections, hashlib, json, sqlite3, subprocess, sys
CLONE = "/tmp/gov-os-assessment-B/repo"
sys.path.insert(0, CLONE + "/src")
from gov.guard.heldout import CONFIG_REL, SETTINGS_REL  # constants only; the files are never opened

db = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{CLONE}/.gov-runtime/store.db?mode=ro", uri=True)
tables = [r[0] for r in db.execute("select name from sqlite_master where type in ('table','view') order by name")]
print("tables:", tables)
files = [r[0] for r in db.execute("select path from lexical_file")] if "lexical_file" in tables else []
chunk_rows = db.execute("select path, count(*) from lexical_chunk group by path").fetchall()
chunks = dict(chunk_rows)
vec = dict(db.execute("select c.path, count(*) from semantic_vector v join lexical_chunk c on c.chunk_id = v.chunk_id group by c.path").fetchall())
tracked = subprocess.run(["git", "-C", CLONE, "ls-files", "-z"], capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.split("\0")
tracked = [t for t in tracked if t]
def ns(p):
    if "/" not in p: return "<root files>"
    top = p.split("/")[0]
    if top == "governance": return "governance/" + p.split("/")[1] if p.count("/") >= 2 else "governance"
    if top == "template": return "template/" + "/".join(p.split("/")[1:3])
    return top
agg = collections.OrderedDict()
for p in sorted(set(tracked) | set(chunks)):
    a = agg.setdefault(ns(p), [0, 0, 0, 0, 0])
    a[0] += p in tracked; a[1] += p in chunks; a[2] += chunks.get(p, 0); a[3] += p in vec; a[4] += vec.get(p, 0)
print(f"{'namespace':40s} tracked indexed chunks embedded_files vectors")
for k, a in sorted(agg.items()):
    print(f"{k:40s} {a[0]:7d} {a[1]:7d} {a[2]:7d} {a[3]:7d} {a[4]:7d}")
tot = [sum(a[i] for a in agg.values()) for i in range(5)]
print("TOTAL", tot)
print("CONFIG_REL tracked:", CONFIG_REL in tracked, "indexed chunks:", chunks.get(CONFIG_REL, 0), "vectors:", vec.get(CONFIG_REL, 0))
print("SETTINGS_REL tracked:", SETTINGS_REL in tracked, "indexed chunks:", chunks.get(SETTINGS_REL, 0), "vectors:", vec.get(SETTINGS_REL, 0))
# tracked, governance-class files that are not indexed (gitleaks or other) - labels only
missing = [p for p in tracked if p not in chunks]
print("tracked but not indexed:", len(missing))
by = collections.Counter(ns(p) for p in missing)
print(dict(by))
# register: how many records share its path, and which id one path maps to
recs = db.execute("select id, type, status from records where path = 'docs/DECISION_REGISTER.md'").fetchall()
print("records with the register's path:", len(recs), "statuses:", dict(collections.Counter(r[2] for r in recs)))
EOF

task: Independent assessment, October 2026, lens B (memory and retrieval, measured). I ran 20 real questions through `gov retrieve` and `gov context` in my own clone of `fecb870c` and judged the results.
status: DONE
work_completed: Three full rebuilds in the clone (R1 11 min 47 s, R2 3 min 52 s, R3 3 min 54 s). The 20 questions ran four times: A, B and C on one index, D after a rebuild. The 10 ticket packets ran twice. I also tested freshness after the staged DEC-813..817 batch, a read during a rebuild, each route alone, radius 2 and 3, the code graph, the index embedder, the index composition and a resume after compaction (engineer, orchestrator, auditor). I wrote the report, re-read it from the file and checked its figures against the saved runs. That check corrected eight statements: a decision count, a line number, a quote, the stopping reasons, the closure examples, the run-D differences, how daemon folders are made, and the checkpoint counts, which grew from 115 to 119 while I worked.
files_changed: The report, `.gov-runtime/scratch/assessment/2026-10/B-memory-retrieval.md` (744 lines, sha256 2195c19175d79ebf…). Scripts and outputs are in `/tmp/gov-os-assessment-B/`. As a side effect, the code-index tool made one folder of its own, `/tmp/gov-cbm-1000/7772036db37428b7`, which I left in place.
evidence: Raw outputs are in `/tmp/gov-os-assessment-B/runs/` (A, B, C, D, CTX-A, CTX-B, FRESH-stale, FRESH-fresh, RADIUS, resume, attribution.json, codegraph-probe.json, embed-determinism.json, rebuild-1/2/3). Each run has a `summary.jsonl` with stdout sha256 and a digest, and the scripts are in `scripts/`.
tests: No test suite was run. The measured runs were: 80 retrievals (20 × 4), 40 context or brief runs, 10 freshness runs, 2 radius runs, 1 closure run, 2 runs during a rebuild, and the attribution, embedder and code-graph probes. All were run on the clone's own code via `PYTHONPATH=…/repo/src`.
discoveries: Twelve of 20 answers are correct in the first five items (2 of them only from tests), 7 partly and 1 not at all. The governing source is in the first five 13 times. Answers are byte-identical on an unchanged index. Nine of 10 context packets are 42–168 times their 6,000-token ceiling, carry no decision text, and still report ok. Any edit to a tracked file switches the whole index off, and `gov context` hides that loss (the main tree is in this state now). New: the code graph cannot answer callers or impact here, because its query hits the tool's 100k-row limit (117,373 edges) and the tool's error message is dropped. Every register chunk carries the id DEC-812, so superseded decisions are served unmarked. Automatic checkpoints hide the recorded next step. `template/**` has no vectors, and tests hold 78% of all vectors.
risks: F7 is unchecked. If a held-out file is tracked, it sits in the lexical index and could surface in answers (fails open). The guard refused my content-free check twice. F3 blocks W2-37's `gov impact`, and no ticket's allowed paths include `src/gov/codeintel/**`.
lessons: Check every report figure against the saved run before publishing: eight statements needed correcting. A content-free digest per run, with sha256 and gold ranks, makes a re-check cheap. On this machine, `ls` shows times in BST, and the run stamps are in UTC.
proposed_decisions: Classification (DEC-809): 15 findings, all "yes" on ordinary work. Two fail open: F4 (fix rides with W2-32, or W2-03 widened, DEC-802) and F7 (only if a held-out file is indexed). None loses work, and 13 are "other". Proposals: give the code-graph fix an owner whose allowed paths include `src/gov/codeintel/**`, and make "callers on this repository" an entry criterion of W2-37 (DEC-803). Add the span-based decision id and filter to W2-32's KPIs. Raise row W2-L253 from low.
unresolved: Whether a held-out or agent-settings file is in the lexical index or in `.gov-runtime/codeintel/files/`: only someone allowed to name the path can check. Whether a code-graph query filtered by edge kind stays under the cap: I counted 77,596 but did not run one.
recommended_next_action: The orchestrator or the owner runs the held-out-path check in recommendation 7. Then the owner decides recommendations 1 to 7, which I judge must be done before any adoption, starting with F1 and F2 through W2-03 and W2-04 and the F3 code-graph owner.
